title: Ponkan (California) citrus: Fruit and Tree Characteristics
metaTitle: Ponkan (California) citrus: Fruit and Tree Characteristics
metaDescription: Ponkan (California) citrus is a satsuma mandarin citrus variety. See its days to harvest, yield, pest ratings, traits and where it grows best.
excerpt: Ponkan (California) citrus is a satsuma mandarin citrus variety. It was registered with the National Seed Industry Council (NSIC) in 2004 as NSIC 2004 Md 03. BPI Bncrdc bred it. Its record notes a yield of 20 kg/tree.

blocks.text: The facts below come from the NSIC registry kept by the Bureau of Plant Industry. Compare it with the others in our [citrus variety finder](/crop-varieties/citrus), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. For the crop itself, read our guide: [fertilizer for fruit trees](/blog/fertilizer-for-fruit-trees).
When does it bear, and how much?

A registered tree variety is described from its mother tree, not from trial plots. The mother tree of Ponkan (California) was about 8 years old and about 1.5 meters tall when it was registered. Its record notes a yield of 20 kg/tree. It bears every year, with fruit in March September. A grafted or marcotted tree bears years sooner than one grown from seed, and its yield climbs as the tree grows.

anee.io keeps the records of each block of trees, from fertilizer to harvest, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside them.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
The registry gives no pest or disease ratings for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.

The pests and diseases that hit citrus fields most often: [citrus greening](/diseases/citrus-greening), [mealybug](/pests/mealybug), [Oriental fruit fly](/pests/oriental-fruit-fly). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.

A fruit of Ponkan (California) weighs about 302 grams, and its shape is obloid (necked). The flesh is orange yellow and soft. Its sweetness measured 11 degrees Brix, the share of sugar in the juice. Most table fruit tastes sweet from about 12 Brix up. The edible part is 75.71 percent of the fruit. The registry notes its fruiting season as March September, bearing annual.
Where and when to plant Ponkan (California) citrus

Sweet oranges and mandarins grow best in the cooler, drier parts of the country. Buy budded trees on a tested rootstock from an accredited nursery, and keep out greening disease. A registered tree variety is a selection from one proven mother tree, and only grafted, budded or marcotted plants carry its traits. A seedling grown from its seed can turn out quite different. So buy from a nursery accredited by the Bureau of Plant Industry, and ask which mother tree the scions came from. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Land preparation for fruit trees](/land-preparation/fruit-tree-land-preparation).

items: Buy grafted or budded plants from an accredited nursery, with the variety name on the tag.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
Plant a few trees first if the variety is new to your area, before you fill the whole farm.
Write down the planting day, inputs and harvest, so you can compare varieties on your own ground. anee.io keeps these records for you.

items.a: The record shows a recorded yield of 20 kg/tree. Your own yield depends on the soil, water, fertilizer and pests on your farm.

items.q: Where can I buy planting material of Ponkan (California)?
items.a: Buy grafted, budded or marcotted trees from a nursery accredited by the Bureau of Plant Industry, so you get the true variety. Ask your provincial agriculture office for the nearest one.
